title: Affine compact-support upper bound
statement:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve and let
$\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf that is punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Then every
compactly supported cohomology group
$H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)$ has weights at most $w+i$. More precisely,
$H_c^0(C,\mathcal F)=0$, $H_c^2(C,\mathcal F)$ is $\iota$-pure of
weight $w+2$, and $H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$.

proof.text: The sheaf $\mathcal F$ is constructible because a lisse sheaf is the single-stratum case of constructibility. Apply [lem-a1-affine-hc0] to obtain $H_c^0(C,\mathcal F)=0$, and [lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure] to obtain purity of $H_c^2(C,\mathcal F)$ of weight $w+2$, including when this group is zero. Apply [lem-zl-affine-curve-range] to obtain $H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$. All three statements have the smooth affine-curve hypotheses in force here; the first two also have the required geometric connectedness and lissity. Only the bound in degree one remains.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: endpoints and range

proof.text: Choose $j:C_0\hookrightarrow C'_0$ and $g:C'_0\to A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ by [lem-a1-finite-map-curve]. Its output is precisely a smooth geometrically connected curve, a dense open immersion with finite complement, and a finite generically etale map, as required by [lem-a1-reduction-composition]. For the constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal K=g_*j_!\mathcal F$, that lemma identifies $H_c^1(C,\mathcal F)$ with $H_c^1(A,\mathcal K)$, compatibly with Frobenius. By [lem-a1-reduction-lisse-pure], on the dense open $a:W_0=A_0\setminus(B\cup g(C'_0\setminus C_0))\hookrightarrow A_0$ the sheaf $\mathcal L=a^*\mathcal K$ is lisse and punctually pure of weight $w$. Here $B$ is the branch locus of $g$; the removed set is finite since $g$ is finite generically etale between curves and $C'_0\setminus C_0$ is finite.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: finite-map transport and lisse locus

proof.text:
Let $b:T_0=A_0\setminus W_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be the reduced closed complement. Use [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ for $\mathcal K$. The compact-support composition/localization clause of [prop-functor-package], applied to $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, then gives the triangle of coefficient complexes
$$R\Gamma_c(W,\mathcal L)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(A,\mathcal K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(T,b^*\mathcal K)\longrightarrow .$$
These are the coefficient complexes of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The maps commute with Frobenius, since the open and closed immersions and $\mathcal K$ are defined over $k_0$, and the localization/composition comparisons have the equivariance asserted by the cited nodes. The long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] includes
$$H_c^1(W,\mathcal L)\longrightarrow H_c^1(A,\mathcal K)\longrightarrow H_c^1(T,b^*\mathcal K).$$
The last group is zero by [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology-positive] with $r=1$: $T_0$ is finite over $k_0$, and $b^*\mathcal K$ is a constructible Weil sheaf in degree zero. No bound on its boundary weights is needed. Exactness therefore gives a Frobenius-equivariant surjection $H_c^1(W,\mathcal L)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(A,\mathcal K)$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: open-closed surjection; repaired positive-degree vanishing

proof.text:
Apply [lem-a1-unramified-at-infinity] to $\mathcal L$ on the dense open $W_0\subset A_0$. Over a finite extension $k'_0=\mathbf F_{q^m}$, it supplies a dense open $v:V_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k'_0}$ and a lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal E$, punctually pure of weight $w$ and unramified at infinity, with a surjection
$$H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(W,\mathcal L).$$
This map is equivariant for Frobenius over $k'_0$. On the right this is the $m$-th power of the original geometric Frobenius. From now until the final descent all weights are measured using $q^m$.

source.place: Proof, fourth paragraph: remove ramification at infinity after constant extension

proof.text:
Let $i:Z_0=\mathbf A^1_{k'_0}\setminus V_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k'_0}$ be the reduced finite complement, and use the ordinary sheaf middle extension $v_*\mathcal E$. Apply [prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] to the dense open immersion of smooth curves $v$. It gives the Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence
$$A_Z:=H_c^0(Z,i^*v_*\mathcal E)\longrightarrow M:=H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)\longrightarrow N:=H_c^1(\mathbf A^1,v_*\mathcal E)\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular $\ker(M\to N)$ is the image of $A_Z$. This sequence is the ordinary-middle-extension sequence, rather than a claim identifying $v_*\mathcal E$ with $Rv_*\mathcal E$.

source.place: Proof, fifth paragraph: boundary exact sequence

proof.text: If $\mathcal E$ has rank zero, it and all its middle-extension stalks are zero, so $A_Z=0$ and the desired bound on $A_Z$ is vacuous. Otherwise its rank is positive: $V$ is a nonempty open of the integral curve $\mathbf A^1_k$, hence connected, and a lisse sheaf has constant rank there. Apply [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] with $X_0=\mathbf A^1_{k'_0}$, $U_0=V_0$ and $\beta=w$. Its hypotheses hold: the ambient curve is smooth separated geometrically connected, the complement is finite, and punctual purity gives $|\iota(\alpha)|^2=(q_s)^w$ at every closed point of $V_0$. Thus the stalks of $i^*v_*\mathcal E$ have weights at most $w$. By [lem-a1-finite-boundary-weights], $A_Z$ has weights at most $w$.

source.place: Proof, sixth paragraph: boundary weights, including the rank-zero case

proof.text: The hypotheses of [thm-a1-line-middle-extension-upper] hold for $v$ and $\mathcal E$, including unramifiedness at infinity. Its degree-one clause gives weights at most $w+1$ on $N$. Put $I=\operatorname{im}(A_Z\to M)$. The subquotient assertion [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds] gives weights at most $w$ on $I$. The same filtration witnesses weights at most $w+1$, since each of its weights is at most $w\le w+1$ in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. Exactness from the preceding boundary-sequence step gives $0\to I\to M\to N\to0$. Apply [lem-a1-extension-bounds] with common bound $w+1$ to conclude that $M=H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)$ has weights at most $w+1$.

source.place: Proof, sixth paragraph: affine-line theorem and extension of the bound

proof.text: The two successive Frobenius-equivariant surjections, followed by the finite-map cohomology identification, make $H_c^1(C,\mathcal F)$ a quotient of $M$ over $k'_0$. By [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds] it has weights at most $w+1$ for $F^m$ and $q^m$. Every eigenvalue on each pure filtration quotient satisfies the bound, and [p-linear-filtration] gives the determinant product for this invariant filtration, so the eigenvalues of the full module are precisely those of its quotient blocks. Hence every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F^m$ satisfies $|\iota(\lambda)|^2\le(q^m)^{w+1}$. Apply [lem-a1-weight-bound-constant-extension] with $b=w+1$ to obtain $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q^{w+1}$ for every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$. To read this as the filtration convention of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], apply [p-linear-triangular] to the automorphism $F$ over the algebraically closed coefficient field to obtain a full invariant flag. Each resulting one-dimensional quotient is pure of the real weight $2\log_q|\iota(\alpha)|\le w+1$. This also covers the zero-dimensional module with the empty filtration.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: quotient bounds and constant-field descent

proof.text: Degree one now has weights at most $w+1$. The degree-two group is pure of weight $w+2$ by the first step, hence has the required upper bound, using its one-step filtration. Every remaining group is zero by that step; the empty filtration gives every upper bound for the zero module in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. These are all integers $i$, proving every clause.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: assemble all degrees

lean.statement: theorem compactlySupportedCohomology_affineCurve_upper [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar k₀))] (a : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hcard : Nat.card k₀ = ringChar k₀ ^ a) (ι : PadicAlgCl l ≃+* ℂ) {C₀ : Scheme.{u}} [C₀.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsAffine C₀] [IsSeparated (C₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (C₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [QuasiCompact (C₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [GeometricallyConnected (C₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (F : WeilSheaf k₀ l C₀) (hF : F.IsLisse) {w : ℝ} (hpure : F.IsPunctuallyPureOfWeight ι.toRingHom w) : (∀ i : ℤ, FrobeniusModule.IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost (ringChar k₀) a l ha (Ne.symm (Fact.out : ringChar k₀ ≠ l)) (PadicAlgCl l) (inferInstance : IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l)) ι (F.compactlySupportedCohomology i) (w + i)) ∧ Subsingleton (F.compactlySupportedCohomology 0).carrier ∧ (F.compactlySupportedCohomology 2).IsPureOfWeightOver k₀ ι.toRingHom (w + 2) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 ∨ 2 < i → Subsingleton (F.compactlySupportedCohomology i).carrier)
